questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of events leading to muscle contraction following acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction?
options: Decrease of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, masking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, masking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled outwards
questions.solution:
Release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.

This action potential spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of calcium ions ($\text{Ca}^{++}$) from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the sarcoplasm.

The increase in $\text{Ca}^{++}$ level leads to the binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin on actin filaments, thereby removing the masking of active sites for myosin.

Utilising the energy from ATP hydrolysis, the myosin head binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a cross bridge.

This pulls the attached actin filaments towards the centre of the 'A' band. The 'Z' lines attached to these actins are also pulled inwards, thereby causing a shortening of the sarcomere, i.e., contraction.

Answer: Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards

questions.q: Troponin controls binding of actin to myosin motor, thereby regulating muscle contraction. Binding of which metal ions to troponin is crucial for this process?
options: Sodium
Magnesium
Calcium
Potassium

questions.q: Which of the following will NOT be triggered by the release of acetyl choline in the synapse at the neuromuscular junction during muscle contraction?
options: Generation of an action potential in the muscles
Release of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Binding of ATP molecules to the myosin head
Shifting of tropomyosin to expose the myosin binding sites on actin filaments

Mitochondria are more in white than in red muscle fibres.
